title: Active-profile sqliteLimit.h constants

scope.rationale: The 20 active immutable profile limits/defaults form one dependency-closed value unit; runtime enforcement remains in separately inventoried callers.
excluded_responsibilities: Runtime limit mutation, allocation enforcement, parser checks, pager checks, and VDBE checks are caller units.

external_source_responsibilities: Production-preprocessor profile selection and runtime consumers; values are independently testable before caller closure.
dependencies.caller_closure: All macro users remain inventoried in the source/dependency/behavior ledgers and receive no closure credit from this unit.

inputs: Pinned build predicates and SQLITE_* profile defines.
outputs: Exact signed/unsigned Zig constants exported by config/build_profile.zig.
contracts.ownership: Immutable compile-time values; no allocation or destruction.
contracts.state_and_results: No runtime state or SQLite result path.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Compile/generation mismatch fails verification; no runtime failure path.

representation_differences: C preprocessor integer tokens become explicitly typed Zig constants with widths/signedness that preserve every active value and ordering constraint.

oracle.protocol: Compile the pinned production C preprocessor and emit selected values; compare exact decimal values and profile feature facts.
oracle.normalization: Decimal textual transport only; no behavioral normalization.

integration.native_call_path: Root and standalone core build modules receive config/build_profile.zig as a named dependency. memory.zig aliases max_allocation_size and pager.zig aliases minimum/maximum/default page size and maximum page count from the one config/limits.zig owner.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Yes for this unit: the duplicate exported limit constants in memory.zig and pager.zig were removed; format-specific numeric literals remain local behavior, not competing limit declarations.

independent_review.notes: The prior independent review at 26b5b94890248d5ead84236dff7811b5d5c0752f failed on duplicate memory/pager owners. The implementation pass removed those declarations and injected the canonical build_profile module into standalone core build modules. A different reviewer must rerun the source, owner, and complete differential review before promotion.

known_blockers: Obtain a fresh independent source/owner/evidence review after the duplicate-owner correction; the implementation pass cannot self-promote.

implementation_spans: upstream/sqlite/src/sqliteLimit.h:1-270 was reviewed in full; selected file hash 6eec89d04286198f5e5f64fcb48c1283446809907f7d650caba40605080c3fe9
The 20 exact active source entity IDs and excerpt hashes in scope cover every selected default/hard-limit token and its selected preprocessor definition
config/limits.zig owns the corresponding explicitly typed values; tools/verify_limits.py compares them with the pinned production preprocessor
callers: SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH: active consumers in btree.c, func.c, main.c, printf.c, vdbe.c, vdbeaux.c, vdbemem.c, and wherecode.c; sqliteLimit.h lines 23 and definition guards are profile selection, not runtime consumers
SQLITE_MIN_LENGTH: main.c:3070-3071 validates runtime changes
SQLITE_MAX_ALLOCATION_SIZE: malloc.c:298/515 and vdbemem.c:1470-1472 enforce allocation/string bounds; sqliteLimit.h:42/45-46 are compile-time guards
SQLITE_MAX_COLUMN: build.c:1084-1085/2197 and main.c:2966/3009-3010/3047 initialize and enforce column limits
SQLITE_MAX_SQL_LENGTH: main.c:2965/2985-2992/3046 initializes and constrains SQL length; sqliteLimit.h:94/108 documents indirect parser/expression coupling
SQLITE_MAX_EXPR_DEPTH: expr.c, parse.y, resolve.c, select.c, sqliteInt.h, and main.c references gate expression-depth fields and walkers
SQLITE_MAX_PARSER_DEPTH: main.c:2976/3049 initializes the parser-depth category; sqliteLimit.h:95 is explanatory coupling
SQLITE_MAX_COMPOUND_SELECT: main.c:2968/2994-2995/3050 initializes and bounds compound terms
SQLITE_MAX_VDBE_OP: main.c:2969/2997-2998/3051 initializes the currently unenforced VDBE-op limit
SQLITE_MAX_FUNCTION_ARG: main.c:1967/2970/3000-3001/3052 enforces registration and connection limits
SQLITE_DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE: btree.c:2811, pragma.c:575, and prepare.c:326/329 consume the default; os_win references are inactive on the selected Linux target
SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT: main.c:3690 installs the default WAL hook threshold
SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED: build.c, main.c, and sqliteInt.h references size and enforce attached-database state
SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER: main.c:2973/3056 and sqliteInt.h:2962/2970 initialize the category and select Expr storage
SQLITE_MAX_PAGE_SIZE: btree.c, pager.c, wal.c, and test_multiplex.h references enforce page/header/frame bounds; sqliteLimit.h:204-205 forcibly retires overrides
SQLITE_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE: pager.c:4802/5003/5011 consumes the default; os_win references are inactive; sqliteLimit.h:216-223 clamps it to maximum page size
SQLITE_MAX_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE: pager.c:5011-5025 chooses device-aware defaults; sqliteLimit.h:231-237 clamps it between default and maximum page sizes
SQLITE_MAX_PAGE_COUNT: pager.c:5095 installs the default maximum database page count
SQLITE_MAX_LIKE_PATTERN_LENGTH: main.c:2972/3006-3007/3055 initializes and validates the LIKE/GLOB pattern category
SQLITE_MAX_TRIGGER_DEPTH: main.c:2974/3012-3013/3057 initializes and validates recursive trigger depth
callees: These are immutable object-like macros and have no runtime callees or ownership transitions
SQLITE_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE and SQLITE_MAX_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE preprocessor clamps depend on SQLITE_MAX_PAGE_SIZE; all three exact values are in this unit
Runtime mutation and enforcement callers are explicitly excluded and remain independently inventoried rather than receiving closure credit here
assertions_branches_cleanup: Pinned empty configure arguments select all #ifndef defaults; SQLITE_MAX_PAGE_SIZE is forcibly undefined and reset to 65536
Compile-time guards cap allocation size at 2147483391 and columns at 32767; page default clamps preserve default_page_size <= max_default_page_size <= max_page_size
The selected constants contain no runtime branches, assertions, allocation, cleanup, locks, callbacks, or I/O; behavioral_block_ids is therefore empty

upstream/sqlite/test/pagesize.test, pager1.test, filefmt.test, io.test, wal.test, crash6.test, and crash8.test cover maximum/default page-size consequences
upstream/sqlite/test/attach.test, bind.test, func.test, select7.test, triggerC.test, bigrow.test, and printf.test provide focused limit consumers
tools/verify_limits.py and config/limits.zig cross-limit tests are the native profile-value controls; caller semantics remain separate units
